statement.text:
Let G be an extension of a normal elementary abelian subgroup A by
an elementary abelian group B ∼   = G/A such that A contains an element a with
CB (a) = 1. Is it true that the rank of the subgroup Z(⟨a, B⟩) ∩ (⟨a, B⟩)′ is at most
the rank of B?                                                           V. I. Zenkov
  ∗ No, not always. Let A = F [x, y]/I 3 be the additive group of the quotient of the
polynomial algebra F3 [x, y] by the ideal I 3 , where I is the ideal generated by x, y.
Let B be the group of automorphisms of A generated by multiplication by 1 + x and
1 + y. Let G = A ⋊ B. For a = 1 ∈ A we have CB (a) = 1B . For H = ⟨a, B⟩ we have
Z(H) ∩ H ′ = + ⟨x2 , xy, y 2 ⟩, which has rank 3, while the rank of B is 2. (P. Monticone,
Letter of 21 March 2026; see also https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/
wp-content/uploads/2026/03/solution_21_150-3.pdf.)
